title: Add UNIQUE(character_id) to active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state so state upserts work
description:
State upserts fail at runtime: the DAL saves for active buffs, spell slots and the round counter use `ON CONFLICT(character_id) DO UPDATE`, but migration 003_state.sql creates active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state with only `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` and no UNIQUE constraint on character_id. SQLite rejects every such upsert with "ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint". Desired: each of the three tables holds at most one row per character, and the existing upserts work unchanged.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12, autonomous; supervisor-confirmed evidence)
- Fix in the schema, not in the queries: add a NEW migration (next number after 005); never edit 003.
- The migration first dedupes existing rows per character_id, keeping the row with the highest id (the latest write), then adds a UNIQUE index on character_id for active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state.
- Remove the 9 `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT(character_id) ...")` DAL tests added by critical-518.3 (PR #13, branch feat/518.3-backfill-tests) in buffdal (7) and spelldal (2) tests. Hence blocked by critical-518.3: stack on that branch or start after it is merged.
- NOT in scope: the nat-1 / nat-20 `t.Skip("bug?: ...")` in combatsvc tests (separate rules decision, handled by the supervisor with the user).

## Current behaviour
SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber always fail, which breaks Activate / Dismiss / Trigger buff, Next Round, Cast spell and Reset slots. Reproduced live (dev-518-6): POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB -> 500 "save slots: upsert spell_slots: ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint".

## Key interfaces
- New migration file under the sqlite migrations dir, e.g. `006_state_unique_character.sql`: per table `DELETE FROM <t> WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM <t> GROUP BY character_id);` then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS <t>_character_id_uq ON <t>(character_id);`.
- The migration runner splits files on semicolons and executes statements one by one (no wrapping transaction), recording the file in schema_migrations only after all succeed: keep every statement idempotent and free of semicolons inside literals/comments.
- DAL query files (buffs.sql, spells.sql) and the BuffStore / spell-slot store ports stay unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New migration exists; 001-005 are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] On a fresh DB, SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber succeed on first insert AND on a second save for the same character (row updated, still exactly one row).
- [ ] On a DB that already holds duplicate rows per character_id in any of the three tables, migrating keeps only the highest-id row per character and then creates the unique index (covered by a test that seeds duplicates before applying the new migration, or an equivalent migrate test).
- [ ] Re-running migrations on an already-migrated DB is a no-op (no error).
- [ ] The 9 buffdal/spelldal `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT ...")` tests are un-skipped and pass.
- [ ] `just generate` run; any change in generated bob output (models/factory/queries) committed, and the CI generated-code check passes.
- [ ] Manual or HTTP-level check: POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB no longer returns 500.
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Tests
buffdal and spelldal DAL tests (the 9 un-skipped ones), plus a migration test for the dedupe-then-index path on pre-existing duplicates.

## Risky
Yes: migration on existing data (deletes duplicate rows) and buff / spell-slot / round-counter state semantics. Needs review per the workflow doc ("Migrations and DAL", "State integrity").

## Parallelism
Adds a migration touching active_buffs, spell_slots, round_state: do not run in parallel with another item adding a migration on those tables or changing bob generated output.

## Out of scope
- Changing the upsert queries or the store ports.
- The nat-1 / nat-20 combat skips.
- Merging the three tables or moving state into the characters table.

title: Decide fly.io hosting shape: access control, topology, backups
description:
Decisions needed before any fly.io work. The PRD says 'no authentication, Tailscale is the security boundary'; a public fly.io URL breaks that.

Questions for the user:
1. Access control: (a) shared-secret/basic auth at the edge, (b) fly private networking + WireGuard/Tailscale only (no public ingress), (c) real login. Recommendation: (a) or (b); the app has no user model and is a single-character personal tool.
2. Topology: one container where the Go API also serves the built web assets (simplest on fly: one machine, one volume), vs. separate api and nginx apps as in docker-compose. Recommendation: single container.
3. SQLite on fly: single machine + fly volume (no horizontal scale, which is fine). Backup via fly volume snapshots only, or Litestream to object storage? Recommendation: snapshots first, Litestream if the data matters.
4. Environments: production only, or also a staging app deployed from PRs?
5. Budget/region constraints.

title: Rulebooks reference: PHB + DMG as agent-readable docs in a private repo
description:
The user's request (2026-10-13, verbatim): "we should have the phb and the dmg in the repo in documentation in a format suitable for agents to refer to. ideally with some kind of indexing to avoid wasting tokens. what do you propose." Sources: https://archive.org/details/player-s-handbook-2nd-edition-2101 and https://archive.org/details/add2nddungeonmastersguidetsr2100

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- ceffo/critical is PUBLIC and the books are WotC copyright, so no rules text goes into critical. The converted text lives in a separate PRIVATE repo, ceffo/critical-rulebooks.
- critical worktrees reach it through a sibling clone at the fixed path ~/code/critical-rulebooks (no submodule: `git worktree add` doesn't init submodules). critical gets only a `just rulebooks` recipe and a pointer in AGENTS.md / docs/agent-workflow.md.
- The supervisor creates the repo (`gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`) and pushes the private repo's work straight to its `main` after its `check` passes. No PRs in the private repo. The critical item is a normal PR.
- The raw archive.org OCR (`*_djvu.txt`, plus the PHB `_page_numbers.json`) is committed under source/. PDFs are fetched on demand by a script, never committed.
- INDEX.md: one line per chapter/section/spell/table PLUS every entry from both printed book indexes, each resolved to `term | book p.N | path`. Agents grep it, never read it whole.
- No seed-shaped spell export: the vodabois scrape stays the app's spell catalog source of truth. PHB spell files carry their stat block as frontmatter only.
- Books in scope: the PHB and DMG only. The layout takes another <book>/ later without rework.
- Not MVP (Saturday hard cut): P3, outside critical-qki.

## Private repo gate (instead of `just validate`)
A `check` script in critical-rulebooks: rerunning the conversion gives byte-identical output; every path in INDEX.md exists; every printed-index page resolves to a file; spot terms ("surprise", "THAC0", "Magic Missile") each give at least one INDEX line.

## Children
1 repo + script + sections + INDEX; 2 per-spell files; 3 hand-checked tables; 4 critical pointer + recipe.

title: Create critical-rulebooks: OCR source, conversion script, PHB/DMG section files, INDEX.md with the printed indexes
description:
Create the private repo ceffo/critical-rulebooks and a reproducible conversion of the PHB and DMG (archive.org OCR) into section-sized Markdown files with a grep-able INDEX.md. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
See the parent epic. The supervisor runs `gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`, clones it to ~/code/critical-rulebooks and gives the developer a worktree of it. The developer commits there and the supervisor pushes to main once `check` passes (no PR).

## Current behaviour
Nothing exists. Supervisor's sample of the archive.org `*_djvu.txt` OCR (PHB ~1.5 MB, DMG ~1.2 MB): the prose is clean. Problems: line-break hyphenation ("unerr- ingly"), stray quotes ("Tenser’'s"), running headers/footers and page numbers inline, tables mangled. Both books have a printed index (term -> page). The PHB item also has `_page_numbers.json`.

## Key interfaces
- Repo layout: `source/` (raw djvu.txt + page_numbers.json, committed as downloaded), `scripts/` (convert, fetch-pdfs, check), `phb/chNN-<slug>/<NN>-<section-slug>.md` (or `phb/chNN-<slug>.md` when a chapter is small), `dmg/...` the same, `INDEX.md`, `README.md` (how to regenerate, how agents should use it).
- Each section file: a few thousand tokens at most; starts with `# <heading>` and a line `Source: PHB p.N-M`. Split at the book's own section headings, keep the book's wording.
- INDEX.md lines: `term | PHB p.N | phb/...md` (sorted, one entry per line, no prose). It contains every chapter and section heading plus every printed-index entry of both books, each resolved to the file holding that page. Unresolvable entries go to a list in README, never dropped silently.
- Cleanup: de-hyphenate across line breaks (keep real hyphens), normalise quotes, strip running headers/footers/page numbers (record page breaks as `<!-- p.N -->` comments so pages stay resolvable).
- Tables: this item leaves them as the OCR has them, fenced and marked `<!-- TABLE: unverified -->`. Item 3 replaces them.
- `scripts/check` as defined in the epic.
- Language/tooling: anything that runs offline on this machine (Python 3 stdlib preferred); no network in convert.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Private repo exists with source/, scripts/, README.md; the source files are byte-identical to archive.org's.
- [ ] Running the conversion twice gives identical output (`check` proves it).
- [ ] Every PHB and DMG chapter is split into section files, none over ~4k tokens (check reports the largest).
- [ ] No hyphenation artefacts or running headers in a sample of 10 random files (listed in the handoff).
- [ ] INDEX.md resolves every section heading and every printed-index entry of both books; unresolved ones listed in README with the reason.
- [ ] `grep -i surprise INDEX.md` and `grep -i thac0 INDEX.md` each give lines pointing at existing files.
- [ ] `check` passes.

## Out of scope
Per-spell files (item 2), hand-checked tables (item 3), anything in critical (item 4), other books, seed data.

## Notes
Not risky (docs/tooling, no app code). Sonnet. No generated code in critical.

title: One file per PHB spell (Wizard, Priest) with stat-block frontmatter, indexed
description:
Split the PHB spell chapters (Wizard and Priest, Appendices) into one file per spell, with the stat block as YAML frontmatter, and add them to INDEX.md. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- Frontmatter only; NO seed-shaped JSON/YAML export. The app's spell catalog source of truth stays the vodabois scrape (seeds/spells.json in critical); don't touch critical's seeds.
- Pushed by the supervisor to the private repo's main after `check` passes.

## Current behaviour
After item 1, the spell descriptions sit in the PHB appendix section files with the stat blocks as OCR prose.

## Key interfaces
- Path: `phb/spells/{wizard,priest}/<level>/<slug>.md`, slug = lowercase English name with hyphens (e.g. `phb/spells/wizard/1/magic-missile.md`).
- Frontmatter keys: `name`, `class` (wizard|priest), `level`, `school` (list; wizard) or `sphere` (list; priest), `reversible`, `range`, `components`, `duration`, `casting_time`, `area_of_effect`, `saving_throw`, `page`. Values copied as printed (strings), not interpreted.
- Body: the spell description, cleaned like item 1.
- INDEX.md: one line per spell, `<Name> (Wizard 1) | PHB p.N | phb/spells/wizard/1/magic-missile.md`. The printed-index spell entries now point at the spell file, not the appendix section.
- `check` gains: every spell file's frontmatter has every key; the count per class and level is reported.
- The appendix section files from item 1 either keep only the non-spell text, or are replaced by the spell files; no spell text appears twice.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every PHB Wizard and Priest spell has exactly one file; `check` prints the counts per class/level, and they match the PHB's spell lists (the per-level lists in the appendices). Mismatches are listed in README.
- [ ] Frontmatter is valid YAML with all keys for every file.
- [ ] `grep -i "magic missile" INDEX.md` gives the spell file; Priest "Cure Light Wounds" the same.
- [ ] Reruns are byte-identical; `check` passes.

## Out of scope
Comparing against critical's seeds/spells.json (a later item if the user wants it), French names (critical-qki.24), DMG magic items, tables.

## Notes
Not risky. Sonnet. Blocked by item 1 (needs the repo, the script and the cleanup).

description:

## Key interfaces
- `tables/<book>-<slug>.md`, one table per file: `# <Table N: title>`, `Source: PHB p.N`, a Markdown table, footnotes as printed.
- Section files keep a one-line link to the table file instead of the OCR table.
- INDEX.md: one line per table, `Table N: <title> | PHB p.N | tables/phb-....md`.
- `check` gains: no `TABLE: unverified` marker left among the listed tables; every table file is linked from INDEX.md.

Changing critical's seeds or rule_tables.json (if a mismatch with critical's seeds is found, report it to the supervisor for a separate item), other books.

title: Point critical's agents at the rulebooks: just rulebooks recipe and the INDEX-first usage rule
description:
Make the private rulebooks clone available to every critical worktree and tell agents how to use it cheaply. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- Sibling clone at the fixed path ~/code/critical-rulebooks, shared by every worktree (no submodule).
- critical is PUBLIC: no rules text, no excerpts, only the path, the recipe and the usage rule.

## Current behaviour
No reference to the rulebooks; agents answer rules questions from docs/backend.md, the ADRs and memory.

## Key interfaces
- `just rulebooks`: clones git@github.com:ceffo/critical-rulebooks.git to ~/code/critical-rulebooks if it is missing, otherwise `git pull --ff-only`. Prints a clear message and exits non-zero without access (e.g. a public user without the private repo); it never runs as part of `just validate` or `just dev`.
- AGENTS.md + docs/agent-workflow.md (a short "Rulebooks" section; agent-workflow.md is where the agents read project specifics): for rules questions, `grep -i '<term>' ~/code/critical-rulebooks/INDEX.md` first, open only the file it names, never read whole chapters or INDEX.md whole. If the clone is missing, run `just rulebooks`; if that fails, say so instead of guessing the rule. The PHB/DMG text is a reference; the project's decided rules (ADRs in docs/adr, user rulings) win where they differ.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `just rulebooks` clones when absent and fast-forwards when present (try both by hand); it fails cleanly without access.
- [ ] AGENTS.md and docs/agent-workflow.md hold the pointer and usage rule above, no book text.
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Out of scope
The private repo's contents (items 1-3), any CI access to the private repo.

## Notes
Not risky (docs/tooling). Sonnet. Blocked by item 1 (the repo and INDEX.md must exist so the recipe and the grep example work). It touches different repos from items 2 and 3, so it can run in parallel with them.

description: Consume-item cast mechanic: the web spells panel re-implements the server's eligibility rule to list items. Expose eligible items from the server (spellbook info or an endpoint) and drop the client filter (no game logic in the frontend). Found during critical-rrv.

title: Concurrent pops (undo/void/reroll) from two tabs return 500 (SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT) instead of 409
description: SQLite WAL deferred transactions: two clients popping the same top at once both read it; the second's write upgrade fails with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT -> 500. No double pop or corruption. Fix: BEGIN IMMEDIATE for pop transactions (actionlogsvc Undo/Void/VoidLatest, initiative reroll), or map busy to 409 centrally. Test with two concurrent pops. Found in the critical-kiv.2 review.

description:
Redesign the main screen of Critical from the v3 design handoff (`.local/mockups/design_handoff_critical_dashboard/`), as a responsive dashboard rather than a pixel copy.

User's words (2026-10-14): "look at @/home/moncef/code/critical/.local/mockups/design_handoff_critical_dashboard/README.md prepare the work into tickets. note that the instructions say to adopt this pixel for pixel. this is not desirable. make sure this is still responsive design. we're not targetting mobiles screen size just yet but it should look good on a large high density browser as well. use /design-taste-frontend to guide you"

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)

- Visual system: Nocturne tokens and the 6 ambiances (Arcane violet default), Inter + Phosphor icons (lucide and Geist removed), with the design-taste-frontend house rules applied (no gradients, no tiny tracked caps, tone steps instead of hairlines, tabular figures).
- Responsive: clamped columns, fluid type; 1280 to 2560 CSS px, full width at 2560 (no max-width). Mobile out of scope: no mobile items.
- Server returns structured data, never text; the frontend localises (en + fr). No client-side game logic or game state ("this thing will be multiplayer one day"). Per-device display prefs (language, light/dark, ambiance) stay in localStorage; dice favourites and the attack form's last choices live on the server.
- Undo = pop the newest log entry on the server (existing snapshot/restorer mechanism) with an expected-top id for concurrency; corrections as their own undoable steps come later (P2); no redo.
- Attack against an unknown AC: the server returns the AC hit and the crit threshold as data; the GM answers with the AC or Touché / Raté (no crit then).
- Initiative: plain 1d10 on Next Round, logged, poppable, rerollable. Weapon speed is out of scope.

- Compétences in P1: bard skills and non-weapon proficiencies from the campaign sheet.
- No level-up: XP shows total, progress and ledger only.
- Character details are editable in the app.
- Rules stay as decided in the repo where the handoff differs: no special natural 1 / 20, crits per ADR 0001.

## Out of scope
Mobile layouts; level-up mechanics; weapon speed / initiative modifiers; redo; a client-side snapshot undo.

description:
Roll initiative (1d10, lowest acts first) automatically on every Next Round, log it as its own entry, show it in the turn block, and allow a reroll.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- Plain 1d10, no modifiers. User: "speed will come later, not in scope".
- Rolled on the server through the dice port; its own log entry, poppable like everything else.
- Reroll = pop the initiative entry and roll a new one (server side, one call).

## Current behaviour
No initiative anywhere. `POST /api/round/advance` decrements buffs and logs a round_advance entry.

## Key interfaces
- Round state gains the current initiative (number, or none at turn 0 / out of combat), restorable by a restorer so undo reverts it.
- Next Round: after the round_advance entry, a separate `initiative` log entry `{round, d10}` is recorded (two entries: undo pops initiative first, then the advance).
- `POST /api/round/initiative/reroll` (name may differ, resource/action style): pops the current initiative entry if it is the newest and records a new roll; 409 otherwise.
- `GET /api/round` returns `initiative: { value, logEntryId } | null`.
- UI: turn block row "Initiative [value] d10 [reroll]" (tooltip: 1d10, lowest acts first); "Hors combat · l'initiative sera lancée" at turn 0; journal renders the entry from its payload; detail card shows it like a free roll.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0013 "Initiative" (number reserved): steps: (1) on Next Round, roll 1d10 through the dice port; (2) record it as its own log entry after the round advance; (3) lowest acts first (display only); (4) reroll replaces the newest initiative entry; (5) out of combat (round 0) there is no initiative. One named test per step, dice mock with distinct values and exact call counts.
- [ ] Undo after Next Round removes the initiative, a second undo the advance.
- [ ] Reroll refused when another entry is newer.
- [ ] Turn block shows the value and the reroll button; e2e covers next turn -> initiative appears -> reroll changes the entry.
- [ ] Common UI acceptance criteria.

title: Architectural Improvement
close_reason: Architectural Improvement epic complete. Deepened the codebase by introducing type-safe Effect Engine, Roll Trace module, and the Actor module for centralized orchestration. Project is now more robust, testable, and easier to navigate.

title: Actor: remove db field, make pure value type
description:
Actor currently stores *sql.DB internally (actor.go:13), coupling the domain entity to persistence. Every Actor method (TakeDamage, GetHPState, ApplyBuff, etc.) is a thin wrapper that re-passes the same db to package-level functions.

Fix: remove the db field from Actor. LoadActor returns a plain struct with no DB reference. Callers (handlers) call the package-level domain functions directly — no Actor intermediary needed for persistence. Actor methods that are now pure (ApplyBuff, DismissBuff, TriggerBuff) keep their in-memory logic but drop the SaveActiveBuffs call; persistence is the caller's responsibility.

No new interface. No new abstraction. Just delete the field and its wrappers.

Files: api/internal/domain/actor.go, api/internal/handlers/*.go, api/internal/domain/buff_actor_test.go

title: ResolveAttack: pre-aggregate modifiers, decouple from Actor
description:
engine.ResolveAttack (combat.go) reaches into actor.ActiveBuffs mid-calculation to apply modifiers. This means: (a) buff state can diverge between LoadActor and the call, (b) the function does hit resolution + damage + crit + buff aggregation in one 60-line god function with no seam.

Fix: introduce a CombatContext value (pre-computed attack bonus, damage formula, crit threshold, buff modifiers). ResolveAttack takes CombatContext + DiceRoller, returns CombatResult — pure function. The caller (handler or a thin builder) aggregates modifiers before calling. engine/buffs.go ApplyBuffModifiers already produces BuffModifiers; caller computes CombatContext from actor.Stats + BuffModifiers.

Benefit: engine is independently testable without a DB-backed actor. Buff aggregation changes don't touch combat.go.

Files: api/internal/engine/combat.go, api/internal/engine/buffs.go, api/internal/handlers/combat.go

title: Handler boilerplate: extract CharacterContext value struct
description:
Seven handler structs each repeat {DB *sql.DB, CharacterID int64}. This is accidental width — the same pair exists by coincidence, not design.

Fix: introduce a CharacterContext struct (db, characterID) that handlers embed. Constructor: NewCharacterContext(db, charID). Handlers become e.g. type HPHandler struct { CharacterContext }. main.go creates one CharacterContext and embeds it into all handlers.

No interface. No behavioral change. Eliminates the repeated field pair and makes main.go construction obvious.

Files: api/internal/handlers/*.go, api/main.go

title: SaveCategory: move from engine to domain, decouple HTTP from engine types
description:
engine.SaveCategory is defined in api/internal/engine/saves.go but used directly in the HTTP request struct in handlers/rolls.go:21. This leaks engine internals into the HTTP contract — renaming or restructuring SaveCategory would break the API.

Fix: define a SaveCategory string type (or reuse engine's constants) in the domain package. The handler decodes the domain type; engine.ResolveSavingThrow accepts the domain type or the handler translates domain → engine before calling. The HTTP contract is decoupled from engine internals.

Files: api/internal/engine/saves.go, api/internal/handlers/rolls.go, api/internal/domain/types.go

User's words (2026-10-12): "we will postpone the deployment epic. what we'll focus first is getting an mvp set of features that I can use in my next D&D game next Saturday. Currently, we have pretty much nothing. Combat computation is grossly incomplete, UI is pretty much unusable, spells do nothing, damage ledger is barely a thing etc etc. we need to chart our way to something usable"

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Must-haves for Saturday (P1 + label `mvp-saturday`): real character data; attack with real weapons; spells with effects; buffs + rounds that affect rolls; daily spell selection respecting the PHB Bard table; one combat log / HP ledger with a good UI; any action correctable (HP entries, casts, Next Round, buff edits); Stoneskin/Mirror Images, ammo by arrow type, charged items. Everything else: P2 in this epic, after Saturday (hard cut).
- Device: laptop only, desktop layout. UI: redesign around a combat round.
- Corrections: ONE append-only action log; each entry stores before/after state snapshots; amend/void are audited events. The log is also the combat log.
- Character data source of truth: the user's Google Sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M07XTZmYA_OwjT6iKZrP9EgX-fI4FQW27I1Vm_aP2Zg). Existing seeds are NOT valid.
- Rules source: PHB 2e text on archive.org; the agent-friendly format is the DjVu plain text: https://archive.org/download/player-s-handbook-2nd-edition-2101/Player%20s%20Handbook%20%282nd%20Edition%29%202101_djvu.txt
- No special natural rolls (nat 1 does not auto-miss, nat 20 does not auto-hit).
- Crit: keep the house rule (D20 - D100 >= needed); multiplier stays x2 as a labelled placeholder; the real xN table is a needs-info item (it is in neither the PHB nor POCT).
- Power Gem effects (+5 weapon, x2) apply ONLY while effective STR is 18; the Bard's base STR is 12, so STR comes from Strength-type spells, often cast on the Bard by other party members.
- i18n: string keys, en + fr, for UI strings and spell names; spell descriptions stay English.
- Weapons and items live in DB tables seeded from JSON; in-app editing after Saturday.
- Review relaxed for this epic (pre-MVP, the user QAs): only the action log and attack math items are `risky`.

## Phase scope
This epic redraws docs/all.md "Phase 1 Scope" (saves, spell lookup, inventory counters are now in); the character-seed item updates the doc.

title: i18n foundation: en/fr string keys for the UI and spell names
description:
Every UI string goes through translation keys with English and French catalogues, and the user can switch language in the app. Spell names will also be translated via keys (filled by the spellbook item), so the key scheme must support a spell namespace.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- "proper i18n management. we refer to strings with keys, we support both en and fr" (user).
- Scope before Saturday: UI strings + spell names. Spell descriptions stay English (no French source).

## Current behaviour
All strings are hard-coded English in the React panels.

## Key interfaces
- A standard React i18n library (e.g. react-i18next), catalogues per language, namespaces at least `common` and `spells`.
- Spell name key = the spell's stable id from the spell database; missing fr key falls back to the English name.
- Language toggle persisted locally (presentation preference only, no API change).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every user-visible string in the current panels comes from a key; none left hard-coded (lint rule or a test that fails on literals if practical).
- [ ] en and fr catalogues complete for the current UI; the toggle switches live and survives reload.
- [ ] A helper to render a spell name by id that falls back to English.
- [ ] docs/frontend.md documents the key convention and namespaces.
- [ ] `just validate` green.

## Tests
Frontend typecheck/build; a small unit test for the spell-name fallback.

## Out of scope
French spell descriptions; translating the spell database. The redesign (separate item) will add new keys.

Not blocked by anything; web-only, can run in parallel with the seed and action-log backend items. Conflicts on files with the combat-screen redesign, which comes after it.

title: Cast spells with effects, and apply spells cast on the Bard by others
description:
Casting a spell does something: uses the slot, shows the spell text, applies its buff or rolls its damage; and spells cast on the Bard by other players can be applied too. Everything is recorded and voidable.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Effects come from seeds/spell_effects.json (extraction item); low-confidence spells only show their text and let the user add a manual buff.
- "spells can and will be cast on the Bard by other players in the party" (user): applying a received spell needs the caster's level and uses no slot.
- Un-cast = void the log entry: slot back, buff removed, damage entry voided.

## Current behaviour
Cast marks the slot used; nothing else.

## Key interfaces
- `POST /api/spells/{slot}/cast` returns a CastResult: spell text, applied buff (with rolled duration/charges, e.g. Stoneskin 1d4+level/2 layers), or damage breakdown (dice by caster level 15 with caps, save type/effect noted for the DM), plus the log entry id.
- `POST /api/spells/receive` {spell id, caster level}: applies the buff effect to the Bard, no slot.
- Casting and receiving write one log entry with before/after snapshot (slots + buffs).
- Spells tab: Cast shows the result card; "Spell cast on me" picker searching the spell database by name (en/fr).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Haste, Strength (received from a party wizard, caster level input), Stoneskin, Mirror Image, Fireball, Magic Missile behave per their seed entries; table-driven tests with injected dice.
- [ ] Receiving Strength that brings effective STR to 18 activates Power Gem effects on the next attack.
- [ ] Voiding a cast restores the slot and removes the buff.
- [ ] `just validate` green.
- [ ] Playwright specs (per critical-qki.16 conventions) cover this item's UI acceptance criteria; `just e2e` green; screenshot paths listed in the report. (added 2026-10-12, UI testing triage)

## Out of scope
Saving throws for targets (DM's side); area templates; concentration.

Blocked by spell effects seed, buffs v2 and spell preparation. Opus.

title: Use charged items and consumables from the round screen
description:
Use charged items and consumables from the round screen: wand of lightning, fire flasks, the Power Gem's daily Dispel, and see ammo counts.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Must-have for Saturday: ammo by arrow type, charged items (wand 6d6 lightning, fire flasks 5d6, gem big Dispel Magic 1/day).

## Current behaviour
Not tracked anywhere in the app.

## Key interfaces
- `POST /api/items/{id}/use`: decrements atomically, rolls the item's damage (breakdown, save type noted), writes a log entry with before/after snapshot; refuses at 0.
- Long rest resets per-day items (gem Dispel).
- Items tab: counts per item and per arrow type, Use button, result card.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Wand use: 4 -> 3 charges, 6d6 rolled with breakdown; void restores the charge.
- [ ] Using an item at 0 returns `{"error": ...}`.
- [ ] Gem Dispel usable once, reset by long rest.
- [ ] Service tests with injected dice; `just validate` green.
- [ ] Playwright specs (per critical-qki.16 conventions) cover this item's UI acceptance criteria; `just e2e` green; screenshot paths listed in the report. (added 2026-10-12, UI testing triage)

## Out of scope
Firing arrows (the attack item decrements ammo); editing items; recharging.

Blocked by the action log, weapons & items, and the round screen.

title: Crit multiplier table for the house crit rule
description:
Replace the x2 placeholder crit multiplier with the house rule's D100 -> xN table, editable in the app.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Keep the house rule: D20 and D100 rolled together; if D20 - D100 still hits, it's a crit; a second
D100 is looked up in a table giving xN (x2, x3, x4...); multipliers stack multiplicatively (engram
#352).

## Decided by the user (2026-10-12, answers the needs-info questions)
- The table is a **house rule** (not from a book). Its values are unknown until the game: the user
  will ask the DM at the table and enter them in the app **during the game**. So the table must be
  editable in the app, not only a seed file.
- Until the user fills it, the table defaults to one row 1-100 -> x2 (today's placeholder), shown as
  "placeholder" in the breakdown.

## Key interfaces
- Crit table stored in the DB (rows: D100 from, to, multiplier). `GET /api/crit-table`,
  `PUT /api/crit-table` (whole table; refuses gaps/overlaps/ranges outside 1-100/multiplier < 1
  with `{"error": ...}` naming the bad row).
- The attack resolution (qki.7's crit path) looks the second D100 up in the stored table; the
  breakdown shows the roll, the matching range and the multiplier.
- A small editor (settings or the Attack tab): add/remove rows, edit from/to/multiplier, save;
  usable quickly at the table. Changing the table is not a logged game action (no void), but it
  never rewrites past attack log entries.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Default table = 1-100 -> x2, labelled placeholder until edited.
- [ ] Editing and saving a table (e.g. 1-50 x2, 51-90 x3, 91-100 x4) is used by the next crit; the
  breakdown shows the second D100, its range and xN.
- [ ] Invalid tables (gap, overlap, outside 1-100, multiplier < 1) are refused with a clear error and
  the stored table is unchanged.
- [ ] Table-driven tests on range boundaries with injected dice; `just validate` green.
- [ ] Playwright spec (per critical-qki.16 conventions): edit the table, then a crit uses it;
  `just e2e` green; screenshot paths listed in the report.

## Out of scope
Per-weapon tables; logging/voiding table edits.

Risky: rules math + a migration (review).

title: Inventory tab: one item model with stock / charges / daily counts
description:
Replace the item kinds (ammo / charged / consumable) with ONE item model whose only real difference is how its count behaves, and turn the Items tab into an Inventory tab with − / + counts. Adding/editing/removing items and weapons are follow-up items.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- User: "these are all consumables... i don't see your point of splitting them between ammo, charges and consumables. it's just their type." An item = name, free-text **type** label (arrows, flask, wand, gem...), count, optional note, optional mechanics the app handles when filled (effect dice, effect save, **magical bonus** +N, **ammo kind**).
- Count behaviour (user confirmed the table):
  - **stock** (arrows, fire flasks): − and + at the table (use, buy more); stays listed at 0, restockable.
  - **charges** (wand of lightning): − only ("i cannot add charges to a wand"); at 0 the item is gone (removed, logged; voiding the use brings it back).
  - **daily** (Power Gem dispel 1/day): − only; stays at 0; refilled to its daily number at long rest only (not by time fast-forward).
- Ammo: linked to weapons by ammo kind (a bow fires "arrow"; every arrow item with ammo kind "arrow" is offered). The arrow's magical bonus adds to to-hit and damage; one is spent per attack, hit or miss. This already works since critical-qki.7 and must keep working.
- The +N is labelled "Magical bonus" (FR "Bonus magique"), shown "+2".
- Tab named "Inventory" (FR "Inventaire"). Every count change is logged and voidable.

## Current behaviour
itemsvc.Kind ammo|charged|consumable; fields AmmoKind, Count, MaxCount, PerDay, MagicBonus, EffectDice, EffectSave, Notes; seeded from seeds/items.json; Use spends one (logged, `items:<id>` snapshots); long rest refills PerDay items to MaxCount. Items tab: ammo and charged sections, Use button, count.

## Key interfaces
- Migration: `behaviour` (stock|charges|daily) + `type` label replace `kind`/`per_day`; existing rows migrate ammo->stock, consumable->stock, charged+per_day->daily, charged->charges; type derived from the old kind/name. `seeds/items.json` and its loader/schema updated accordingly (seeds stay idempotent). `just generate`.
- itemsvc: `Use` (all behaviours; charges at 0 -> removed), `Restock(id, n)` / count + for stock only (charges/daily rejected), long rest refills daily only. Each change one log entry with `items:<id>` snapshots (removal restorable by void).
- `POST /api/items/{id}/use` (existing), `POST /api/items/{id}/restock` `{count}`; API `Item` JSON exposes behaviour, type, magicalBonus, ammoKind, maxCount; web/src/types match.
- Attack resolver reads magical bonus/ammo kind from the new model (no behaviour change).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inventory tab lists all items (name, type, count, behaviour badge); − uses one; + exists only on stock items and adds one (logged).
- [ ] A wand used down to 0 disappears; voiding that use brings it back with 1 charge.
- [ ] Arrows at 0 stay listed and can be restocked; the attack picker offers only arrows with count > 0.
- [ ] Long rest refills the gem (daily) and nothing else.
- [ ] Existing DB migrates without loss (test on a DB with the old rows); fresh seed works.
- [ ] Attack with Short Bow +2 and Arrows +1 still adds both to hit and damage and spends one arrow (existing tests pass unchanged in meaning).
- [ ] Go tests (behaviours, removal + void, restock rejection, long rest), migration test, Vitest, e2e step. `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Adding/editing/removing items (next item) and weapons (separate item); encumbrance; prices.

Risky: yes (migration, item state, attack ammo). Model: Opus. Not in parallel with qki.14, qki.28, qki.29, qki.30.

title: Log saving throws and adjust the latest save on its result card
description:
Saving throws become logged table actions, and the latest save can be adjusted after the roll on its result card: the adjustment changes the outcome, never the d20. Origin: the Bard's "Gaia" fire/lightning protections (+4 to saves vs fire/lightning) and any bonus only known after the roll.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- No special code for Gaia: the protections are ordinary buffs the user adds (see the saved-buffs item); the +4 is applied through this adjustment. No damage types and no arithmetic on damage taken: the HP amount entered is final ("value is after all modifiers; the DM does not always disclose what affected it"). The old ideas (halve fire damage, +4 save display) are dropped.
- "Each save throw should have an optional adjustment on the result card. Adjusting it changes the outcome but not the roll."
- "Everything affecting the game should be logged": a save is an action-log entry (category, d20, buff modifiers, target, pass/fail); voidable from the log like other entries.
- Adjustment = one signed integer with − / + buttons, starting at 0, plus an optional reason (e.g. "Gaia fire"); the log line shows it ("adjusted +4 Gaia fire: FAILED → PASSED").
- Only the latest roll's card is adjustable; older entries are fixed with void + reroll. No reminder line of conditional buff bonuses on the card (active buffs are visible in the buff strip).

## Current behaviour
`POST /api/saves` (combathdl.RollSave -> combatsvc.ResolveSavingThrow) rolls d20 + buff SaveBonus vs the category target and returns a RollResult; nothing is logged. The save result card (ResultCard SaveResult) shows the verdict, d20, target, margin, modifiers. `POST /api/log/{id}/amend` exists for hp_change entries only.

## Key interfaces
- New action-log kind `save` (payload: category, d20, modifiers, target, adjustment, adjustment reason, passed, margin). It changes no state, so it carries no snapshots (or an empty set); void just marks it voided.
- Adjust: e.g. `POST /api/log/{id}/adjust` (or extend amend to `save` entries) with `{adjustment:int, reason?:string}`; the SERVER recomputes pass/fail and margin with the stored d20 (no game logic in the frontend), records an audited correction, returns the updated RollResult. Rejected (409/400) when the entry is not a save, is voided, or is not the latest roll.
- RollResult for saves gains `entryId`, `adjustment`, `adjustmentReason` so the card can adjust.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Rolling a save writes one `save` log entry; it appears in the combat log with category, d20, target and verdict; it can be voided.
- [ ] On the latest save's card, setting the adjustment to +4 with reason "Gaia fire" turns d20 12 vs target 14 from FAILED (margin −2) into PASSED (margin +2); the d20 shown stays 12; the log entry shows the adjustment, reason and the before → after verdict.
- [ ] Setting it back to 0 restores the original verdict (also logged). Natural-roll rules unchanged (whatever ResolveSavingThrow does today for 1/20).
- [ ] Adjusting a non-latest, voided or non-save entry is rejected with a clear error.
- [ ] Go: table-driven tests for the recompute (fail→pass, pass→fail, 0), log payload, rejections; handler/router tests; Vitest for the card; an e2e step (roll a save, adjust, verdict flips, log line). `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Attack target-AC correction (sibling item, same pattern, do it after this one); damage types; conditional buff bonuses applied automatically; adjusting from the combat log.

Risky: yes (new action-log kind and correction semantics, API contract). Model: Opus. Touches the result card and log amend code like the attack-AC item: not blocking, but they can't run in parallel; this one first.

title: Playwright e2e harness: just e2e on a throwaway stack, with smoke specs and docs
description:
Give agents a headless way to prove a UI acceptance criterion: a Playwright e2e harness behind `just e2e` that drives the real app (Go API + Vite) on a throwaway stack, saves screenshots for visual review and traces on failure. Lands before the dashboard redesign (critical-qki.6) so the redesign and every later UI item ship with specs.

User's words (2026-10-12): "i need you or your team to devise a proper UI testing strategy. probably using playwright."

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Lands BEFORE qki.6 and blocks it (P1, mvp-saturday).
- Layers: Playwright e2e against the real API + screenshots as artifacts. No pixel-diff snapshot assertions, no component-test layer for now (vitest from qki.1 stays for units).
- Local only: no CI job yet (separate P3 item under critical-8g1). `just validate` unchanged; `just e2e` is a separate recipe.
- Mandatory per UI work item: Playwright specs covering its UI acceptance criteria, `just e2e` green, screenshot paths listed in the developer report.
- i18n: flow specs run in en; ONE fr smoke spec toggles to French and checks no raw keys are visible.
- Data: the repo's real `seeds/` + a fresh temp SQLite DB per spec file. Specs assert relative changes (HP drops by the damage entered), never hard-coded character values, so the qki.2 reseed does not break them.
- Selectors: getByRole/getByLabel with English accessible names first; `data-testid` only for non-semantic regions (HP value, log entries).
- Artifacts: HTML report, PNGs and traces in `web/e2e-results/` (gitignored); nothing binary committed. The supervisor relays PNG paths to the user.

## Current behaviour
Agents stop at typecheck/build (+ vitest units after qki.1); nobody can verify a panel headlessly; the supervisor tells the user "look at it yourself". The API does not serve the web build; Vite already reads `CRITICAL_API_URL` for its `/api` proxy; the API takes `CRITICAL_DSN`, `CRITICAL_SEEDS_DIR`, `CRITICAL_ADDR`. `just dev` binds fixed ports (:8080/:5173), so it can't be used by parallel worktrees.

## Key interfaces
- `just e2e` (from repo root): builds the API, installs/uses Playwright Chromium, runs the suite; any extra args pass through to `playwright test` (e.g. `just e2e smoke.spec.ts`). A `just e2e-install` (or equivalent first-run step) installs the browser.
- Playwright config in `web/` (specs under `web/e2e/`): Chromium only, viewport 1440x900, `trace: retain-on-failure`, output + HTML report under `web/e2e-results/`.
- A shared fixture that gives each spec file its own stack: API on a free port with a new temp DB under the OS temp dir and `CRITICAL_SEEDS_DIR` = repo `seeds/`, plus a Vite server on a free port whose `/api` proxy targets that API (the proxy target is fixed at Vite start, so either Vite per spec file too or an equivalent that keeps isolation). Processes and temp DBs cleaned up even on failure. Never touches `.dev/` or fixed ports, so two worktrees can run `just e2e` at the same time.
- A screenshot helper: `snap(page, name)` writes `web/e2e-results/screens/<spec>/<name>.png`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `just e2e` runs green from a fresh worktree after `npm ci` (+ the documented browser install step), with nothing else running.
- [ ] Two `just e2e` runs in parallel (e.g. two worktrees) don't collide: free ports, separate DBs.
- [ ] Smoke specs against the CURRENT dashboard: (a) app loads and shows the character's HP; (b) entering damage lowers current HP by exactly that amount without reload; (c) fr smoke: toggle to French, no raw i18n keys visible, screenshot saved.
- [ ] Each spec saves at least one PNG at 1440x900; a deliberately failing assertion leaves a trace zip in `web/e2e-results/`.
- [ ] `web/e2e-results/` and Playwright caches are gitignored; `just validate` does not run e2e and still passes (lint/typecheck include the e2e TS files without breaking).
- [ ] docs/agent-workflow.md updated: "Validation" (UI items must add/extend specs per UI acceptance flow and run `just e2e` green; list screenshot paths in the report), "Running the app for acceptance checks" (`just e2e`, artifacts location), "Review" (visual review uses the e2e screenshots); keep headings stable.
- [ ] docs/frontend.md gets a "Testing" section: layers, selector convention, relative assertions, en flows + one fr smoke, how to add a spec, where artifacts land.

## Tests
The smoke specs themselves; `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
CI job (separate item under critical-8g1); pixel-diff baselines; vitest component tests; specs for the redesign (qki.6 writes its own and may replace the smoke specs' selectors).

Blocked by critical-qki.1 (the fr smoke needs the language toggle; both edit web/package.json). Blocks critical-qki.6. Model: Sonnet (tooling, not a UI-heavy bead). Not risky per the review triggers.

title: Preparing spells must not fail on spells outside the spellbook
description:
Preparing today's spells fails with `{"error": "spell is not in the spellbook: ..."}` when today's
slots hold spells that are not in the Bard's spellbook. The user hit this at the table rehearsal
("can't prepare spells, gets errors that spells not in the spellbook").

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Root cause found by the scoper: the dev DB `.dev/critical.db` predates the real Bard seed (character
  level 9, slots holding old seed spells: Armor, Audible Glamer, Web, ...). Seeds load only into an
  empty DB. The Prepare editor pre-fills its draft with those slot ids, hides them (not in the
  spellbook) and still sends them on Save, so the server refuses the whole request.
- The user runs `just dev-reset` once to get the real seed (accepted: loses test log entries). No
  seed-sync mechanism before Saturday.
- The editor must still cope with unknown prepared spells (any stale or renamed id), not only after
  a reset.

## Current behaviour
`PrepareEditor` initial draft = slot ids (or slug of the slot name); entries not in the spellbook are
not rendered but stay in the draft; `onSave(draft)` sends them; `PUT /api/spells/prepared` returns
ErrNotInSpellbook.

## Key interfaces
- `PUT /api/spells/prepared` unchanged (still refuses unknown ids, error names the id).
- Editor: drafts only spellbook ids; prepared spells that are not in the spellbook are listed once
  as "no longer in the spellbook, will be removed" (i18n en/fr) and are not sent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With slots holding spells outside the spellbook, opening Prepare and saving a valid selection
  succeeds; the unknown spells are shown as removed, not sent.
- [ ] After `just dev-reset`, the character is level 15 and preparing 3 level-1 spells works.
- [ ] Unit/component test for the draft filtering; Playwright spec (per critical-qki.16 conventions)
  covering prepare-with-stale-slot; `just validate` and `just e2e` green.

## Out of scope
Seed sync into existing DBs; spell database cleanup (separate item); the Bard's name (separate item).
Touches the Spells tab like the spell lookup items, but does not block them.

title: Name the Bard Kelsen Balstriel; tests stop pinning campaign seed data
description:
Name the Bard Kelsen Balstriel, and stop tests from pinning campaign data from seeds/.

## Decided by the user (2026-10-13)
- The name is data: change `seeds/character.json` only (the user runs `just dev-reset`).
- First attempt (PR #36, closed by the user) only changed the seed and copied the new name into
  `TestGetCharacter_RepoSeedIsTheCampaignBard`. Wrong: tests must not assert campaign values.
- Since qki.2 (#24), tests load the real `seeds/` and assert its values (name, stats, XP, HP, saves,
  spell effect numbers, rule-table entries). Every data edit then breaks a test. Clean that up now,
  before dark mode.

## Rules for tests
- Service, DAL, adapter and composition tests use their own small fixtures (`testdata/` or values built in
  the test), never `seeds/`.
- Tests on the real `seeds/` check only that the data is well formed: it loads, matches the schema, and
  references resolve (spellbook ids exist in the catalog, effects point to real spells, items reference
  real weapons...). No campaign values asserted.
- e2e: no literal campaign values (name, HP, stats...) asserted; read what the app shows from the
  API/seed at runtime when a value is needed.

## Files reading seeds/ today
characterdal, ruletablesadpt, spellbookadpt, spelleffectsadpt, weapondal tests; composition
(cast_test, composition_test, longrest_test); castsvc and combatsvc tests; storage/sqlite seed_catalog_test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Header shows "Kelsen Balstriel" on a fresh DB; the name appears in no test.
- [ ] No Go test outside the repo-seed integrity tests reads `seeds/`; the integrity tests assert no
  campaign values.
- [ ] e2e specs assert no literal campaign values.
- [ ] Changing a value in a seed (e.g. HP 85 → 80) breaks no test (developer checks it and reverts).
- [ ] `just validate` and `just e2e` green.

title: Dark mode: light/dark/system toggle
description:
Add a dark mode to the web app (user: "UI darkmode").

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- A light / dark / system toggle in the header, remembered in localStorage; the default is system
  (follows prefers-color-scheme, live when the OS setting changes).
- For Saturday (P1).

## Current behaviour
shadcn/Tailwind dark tokens exist (`.dark` class and `@custom-variant dark` in web/src/index.css; a
few `dark:` classes), but nothing ever sets the `.dark` class and there is no toggle.

## Key interfaces

title: Spell lookup: name-first list + detail pane, FR/EN search, Mine/Wizard/Priest/All, level chips, school groups

"the filtering UI is complete garbage. you should have designed this with the user". This design was

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- Use: (1) look up a spell named at the table, (2) plan what to cast from the Bard's own spells. Receive
  keeps its own picker; browsing the catalog is a between-sessions use. Screen: the laptop dashboard (lookup
  tab about 590px wide); phone is not a target.

  grey after it when it exists ("Mains brûlantes · Burning Hands"). French names exist only for the Bard's
  38 spells (all spells = critical-qki.24, P4).
- Layout: a list on top (about 45% of the tab height, scrolls on its own) and a detail pane below (the rest,
  scrolls on its own). The first result is selected automatically while typing; up/down in the search box
  moves the selection; a click selects.
- List row, one line: level (`L3`), name (UI language, other language grey), class chip only when the
  class toggle is on All, school in small text on the right. No stats in rows.
- Detail pane: header = name (FR · EN), class, level, school/sphere, components. Dense two-column stat grid
  (range, duration, area, casting time, save): the value typed at the Bard's level with the raw book text
  in grey next to it (e.g. `210 yd` · 10 yd + 10 yd/level). Description behind an expander, collapsed by
  default (user: "expander for the dull description"), FULL text when opened (no 200-char cut). No action
  buttons.
- Filters (only these): one toggle row `Mine | Wizard | Priest | All`, default **Wizard** (Mine = the
  Bard's spellbook); level chips 0-9, multi-select (none = any); an optional school dropdown. In Priest mode
  that dropdown lists spheres instead of schools. Dropped from the UI: save, casting time, components,
  free-text school, the caster-level box (always the Bard's level).
- School dropdown: the 8 PHB schools (Abjuration, Alteration, Conjuration/Summoning, Divination,
  Enchantment/Charm, Illusion/Phantasm, Invocation/Evocation, Necromancy) + "Other" (Tome of Magic and the
  rest: Dimension, Geometry, Alchemy, Elemental…). A spell matches when any of its listed schools maps to
  the chosen group ("Evocation" -> Invocation/Evocation, "Enchantment" -> Enchantment/Charm,
  "Conjuration"/"Summoning" -> Conjuration/Summoning, "Illusion"/"Phantasm" -> Illusion/Phantasm).
- Sort: level then name; when a search text is set, exact name matches first, then prefix matches, then
  contains (over FR and EN names), each tier level then name.
- No Prev/Next: one scrolling list; the next page (API max 200) loads as the list nears its bottom. The list
  header always shows the true total "N spells"; never truncate silently.
- State: search text, toggle, levels, school and the selected spell survive switching tabs; a page reload
  clears them. One "Reset" link, shown only when something is set.
- Receive ("Spell cast on me") keeps its own compact picker but uses the same name search (FR + EN, same
  ranking). No "cast on me" button in the lookup.

chars, and Prev/Next "Showing 1-50 of N". `GET /api/spells` takes q (EN name), class, level (single), school

- `GET /api/spells` gains: `class=mine|wizard|priest|all` (mine = spells in the Bard's spellbook, already

  key>` for the PHB groups + `other`, `sphere=<name>` for Priest spheres, and a way to match French names:
  the server does not know them, so the client resolves the query against the i18n `spells` catalog (as
  ReceivePanel does) and sends the matching spell ids with their tier (exact/prefix/contains); the server
  ORs them with its EN name match and ranks across both. Exact param shape is the developer's call, written
  in the PR. Response stays `{items,total,page,page_size}`; items keep typed values at the Bard's level.
- A small endpoint or field listing the dropdown options (school groups, spheres) is fine; the spell id stays
  the slug of the English name (spellId).
- Unused filter params (save, casting_time, components, caster_level) may stay in the API; the UI no longer

- [ ] Typing a French name ("mains") finds Burning Hands; the row shows "Mains brûlantes · Burning Hands"

- [ ] Ranking: for "fire", exact/prefix matches ("Fireball", "Fire Trap"...) come before contains matches

- [ ] Toggle defaults to Wizard; Mine shows exactly the spells of the Bard's spellbook (seeds/spellbook.json); Priest and All work; the class

- [ ] Level chips multi-select (L1 + L3 shows only those levels); none selected = any level.
- [ ] School dropdown: "Invocation/Evocation" includes spells listed as "Evocation"; "Other" includes Tome

- [ ] Unfiltered list header reads "885 spells" (or the current catalog total); scrolling to the bottom

- [ ] Up/down in the search box moves the selection; a click selects; the detail pane shows typed values
      at the Bard's level next to the raw text; the description is collapsed by default and shows the full
      text when opened.
- [ ] Switching to another tab and back keeps search, filters and selection; reload clears; Reset appears
      only when something is set and clears everything.
- [ ] Receive picker finds spells by FR and EN with the same ranking as the lookup.
- [ ] Go tests: spellsvc/handler tests for mine, multi-level, school groups (alias mapping), sphere, ranking
      tiers incl. client-supplied FR ids; built from fixtures, not campaign seed values.
- [ ] Playwright spec `lookup` replaced: one test per criterion above, screenshots under
      `e2e-results/screens/lookup/` (search-selected, french-name, mine, levels-1-3, school-evocation,
      priest-sphere, scrolled-to-end, description-open), light and dark theme lookup screenshots refreshed.
- [ ] `just validate` and `just e2e` green.

## Risky
Labelled risky: changes the `GET /api/spells` contract and the search ranking used by two panels.

title: Correct the target AC on the latest attack after the roll
description:
At the table the target's AC is often only known (or corrected by the DM) after the attack is rolled. Let the user correct the target AC on the latest attack's result card: hit/miss and crit are recomputed with the SAME d20 and d100, and the logged attack is amended.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- "Same mechanic will be needed for adjusting the target AC in combat. It is not always known in advance." (same pattern as the save adjustment, critical-qki.14).
- Damage dice are rolled on EVERY attack, even a miss, and stored, so a miss turned into a hit shows its damage without rerolling (user: yes).
- The logged attack entry is amended to the new AC and outcome, audited like an HP amend (user: yes). "Everything affecting the game should be logged."
- Only the latest roll's card is adjustable; older entries: void + reroll.

## Current behaviour
combatsvc.ResolveAttack: needed = EffectiveThac0 − TargetAC; Hit = d20 ≥ needed; IsCrit when d20 − d100 ≥ needed (multiplier from the house crit table); damage dice are rolled only on a hit. The attack is logged (kind `attack`, with ammo snapshots). The attack card shows the target AC read-only.

## Key interfaces
- ResolveAttack always rolls the damage dice and stores them in the result/log payload (shown only on a hit).
- Correct: e.g. `POST /api/log/{id}/adjust` with `{targetAc:int}` for `attack` entries (reuse the endpoint shape from qki.14); the server recomputes hit, margin, crit (row lookup with the stored d100), and damage from the stored dice and stored modifiers; records an audited correction; returns the updated RollResult. Ammo is NOT spent again. Rejected when not the latest roll, voided or not an attack.
- The attack card's target AC becomes an editable number field (− / +); the heading/verdict/damage update from the server response.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A miss vs AC 5 (d20 11, needed 13) becomes a hit when the AC is corrected to 7; damage shown is the dice rolled at attack time (no reroll; dice port called once per attack).
- [ ] A hit can become a miss (damage hidden), and a crit can appear/disappear from the stored d100 per the crit table; nat 1 / nat 20 rules unchanged.
- [ ] The log entry shows "AC 5 → 7: MISS → HIT" and the new damage; voiding it still restores ammo as today.
- [ ] Ammo count unchanged by the correction.
- [ ] Go table-driven tests (miss→hit, hit→miss, crit flip, damage reuse, rejections) that fail on the old code; Vitest for the card; e2e step. `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Adjusting other modifiers after the roll (situational stays pre-roll); adjusting from the combat log; HP of the target.

Risky: yes (rules math: hit/crit/damage; log correction semantics). Model: Opus. Not blocked by qki.14 but touches the same result card and log correction code: run after it, reusing its endpoint pattern.

description:

title: Action log: one append-only log of table actions with audited amend/void
description:
One append-only action log records every table action and lets the user amend or void any entry; it becomes the HP ledger and the combat log. Backend + API only; the redesign item builds the UI on it.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- "damage/healing ledger with good ui. should be able to amend/correct a mistake" (user).
- One action log for all actions (HP change, cast, buff change, Next Round, attack, item use), not per-feature undo.
- Each entry stores before/after snapshots of the state it changed (buffs, slots, round, counters). Voiding an entry restores its "before" state when no later non-voided entry changed the same state; otherwise the void is refused with a clear error (or the user voids the later one first).
- Corrections are audited: amend/void are new events pointing at the original; history shows "amended"/"voided". No in-place edits.

## Current behaviour
hp_events ledger with append + "undo last" only; buffs/slots/round are JSON state rows overwritten in place, no history; nothing records attacks or casts.

## Key interfaces
- Action entry: id, character_id, round, kind (hp_change | cast | buff_change | round_advance | attack | item_use | ...), summary payload (JSON, e.g. full RollResult for attacks), before/after state snapshots, created_at, status derived from correction events.
- Correction event: target action id, kind amend|void, new payload for amend (amend on HP changes: amount and source).
- A domain port other services use to record an action atomically with their state write (same transaction).
- Current HP = SUM of effective HP deltas (amended value, voided = 0), still computed in SQL.
- REST: `GET /api/log` (newest first, with correction status), `POST /api/log/{id}/amend`, `POST /api/log/{id}/void`; existing `POST /api/hp/event` now writes through the log; `/api/hp/undo` = void of the last HP entry.
- Existing hp_events data migrated (new migration file, never edit an applied one).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HP damage/heal recorded as log entries; amend changes current HP and keeps the original visible; void removes its effect.
- [ ] Voiding an entry with snapshots restores the before state; voiding when a later entry changed the same state is refused with `{"error": ...}`.
- [ ] Record + state write are one transaction (test with a failing DAL).
- [ ] Migration applies on an existing dev DB with hp_events data; totals unchanged.
- [ ] Service and DAL tests per docs/backend.md; `just generate` and `just mocks` run; `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Recording casts, rounds, buffs, attacks, items (each feature item plugs into this port); the UI.

Risky: migration + ledger/state semantics.

title: Fast-forward time in decimal hours to expire buffs
description:
Let the user fast-forward game time in decimal hours so long-running buffs count down and expire correctly between fights.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13, interactive, user's answers)
- A "⏩ Time passes" control next to the round controls: the user types decimal hours (0.25, 1.5, 8). 1 round = 1 minute (AD&D), so rounds = floor(hours × 60) (user: round DOWN); the preview "= 90 rounds" shows before confirming.
- Every timed buff loses that many rounds; those reaching 0 expire and show in the usual "expired" notice. Charge-only and untimed buffs are untouched.
- The combat round counter goes to 0 (user: "goes to zero").
- Logged and voidable ("everything affecting the game should be logged").
- Buff badges show hours/minutes for long durations, from 60 rounds up: "150 r · 2 h 30".
- Daily items are NOT refilled by fast-forward (long rest only).

## Current behaviour
buffsvc: Next Round (AdvanceRound) decrements timed buffs by 1 and expires at 0; End combat (ResetRound -> 0) and Set round move the counter and leave buffs alone; all logged with `buffs`/`round` snapshots and restorers. Badges show "N rounds".

## Key interfaces
- buffsvc `PassTime(ctx, characterID, rounds int)` -> (active, expired, round) in one transaction: decrement timed buffs by rounds, expire ≤ 0, round = 0; one log entry (new kind e.g. `time_passed`, payload hours + rounds) with `buffs` and `round` snapshots so void restores both.
- `POST /api/round/pass-time` with `{hours: number}`; the server converts (floor(hours×60)), rejects ≤ 0 or > a sane max (e.g. 720 h) and results of 0 rounds; returns the same shape as Next Round. The preview conversion may be shown client-side but the server is the authority.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 1.5 h = 90 rounds: a buff with 100 rounds keeps 10, one with 60 expires (notice), a charge-only buff is unchanged; the round counter is 0.
- [ ] 0.01 h is rejected (0 rounds) with a clear message; 0.02 h = 1 round.
- [ ] Voiding the entry restores the buffs and the previous round number.
- [ ] Badge: 150 rounds shows "150 r · 2 h 30"; 59 rounds shows rounds only (FR/EN).
- [ ] Go table-driven tests (conversion floor, expiry edge at exactly 0, untimed/charged untouched, void), handler test, Vitest for the badge format, e2e step. `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
An in-game clock / time of day; refilling daily items; spell slot recovery (long rest exists).

Risky: yes (buff/round state semantics, new log kind). Model: Opus. Not blocked, but adds a log kind in shared code: not in parallel with qki.14, qki.28, qki.29 or the inventory items.

title: Effective STR: all Strength bonuses stack up to 18, Improved Strength replaces them (to 23); Power Gem at STR >= 18; str_set removed
description:
The Power Gem's weapon effects (weapon becomes +5, x2 multiplier, or whatever a gem saved buff carries) must apply only while the Bard's effective STR is exactly 18. Today a buff's STR requirement is "at least": at effective STR 19-23 (Improved Strength 1d6+4, cap 23) the gem still gives +5/x2. Found by the rules audit (reports/rules-audit.md, DIVERGES 1, UNTESTED 4).

## Decided in triage
- critical-qki.7 "Decided in triage (2026-10-12)", verbatim: "Power Gem: its weapon effects (+5, x2) apply only while effective STR is 18."
- docs/all.md (Phase 1 scope) and docs/backend.md "Attack Modifiers" say the same ("only at effective STR 18").
- critical-qki.15 (closed 2026-10-13): Power Gem forms are user-made saved buffs (weapon_buff 5, min_str 18, ...), no gem-specific code. So the fix is a generic buff gate, not a gem special case.
- Supervisor brief 2026-10-13: fix per the recorded decision (exactly 18); not re-asked.

## Current behaviour
buffsvc effect engine skips a buff only when `effective STR < MinStr`; nothing caps it above. Tests only check 18 and 19 against an 18 floor.

## Key interfaces
- `BuffEffects` gains an optional upper gate `MaxStr *int` (JSON `max_str`, nil = no upper bound), validated like `min_str` (1-25, and max_str >= min_str when both set). A buff contributes only while `MinStr <= effective STR <= MaxStr`. A Power Gem buff sets min_str = max_str = 18. STR effects themselves stay ungated (as today).
- Flows through everywhere `min_str` does: buff create/edit API, active-buffs JSON + snapshots, saved buff templates, cast effects (casthdl), list responses (`active` false when either gate fails), `web/src/types/buffs.ts`.
- Buff form + saved-buff form expose "Max STR"; the inactive hint reads e.g. "Needs STR 18" when min = max, "Needs STR 18-20" for a range (en + fr keys).
- Existing data: buffs/templates already stored with only min_str 18 keep ">= 18" until the user edits them (no data migration; the JSON columns need no schema change). Say so in the PR body.
- Cite in code comment and commit: docs/backend.md "Attack Modifiers" (Power Gem only at effective STR 18) / qki.7 decision; the ADR item for buffs will absorb it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Table-driven buffsvc test, gem buff (min 18, max 18, weapon_buff 5, multiplier 2) with STR buffs giving effective STR 17, 18, 19 and 23: active only at 18; at 17/19/23 contributes no weapon buff and no multiplier. Fails on the old code at 19 and 23.
- [ ] combatsvc (or composition) attack test at effective STR 19 with the gem: weapon magic is the weapon's own, multiplier 1; dice mocks distinct-valued with exact call counts.
- [ ] Validation: max_str out of 1-25 or below min_str -> 400 with `{"error": ...}`.
- [ ] max_str round-trips through active buffs, snapshots (void restores it), saved templates and the cast path; web types match Go.
- [ ] Buff strip shows the inactive hint at STR 19 for the gem; Playwright spec covers adding a buff with min/max STR 18 and seeing it inactive above 18 (`just e2e` green, screenshot paths in the report).
- [ ] `just validate` green; report ends with a RULES TRACE block.

## Out of scope
The ADRs (separate items); gem forms; any data migration of existing buffs.

Tests: buffsvc table test, combatsvc attack test, buffhdl validation, e2e. No migration, no bob regeneration; mocks only if a port changes.
Risky: rules math + buff state semantics (review). Model: Opus. Touches buffsvc/combatsvc: not parallel with critical-qki.34 or ADR items.

title: Make the SQLite opener wait on locks: busy_timeout 5000 ms and WAL on every connection
description:
The app's SQLite opener sets no busy timeout and uses the default rollback journal, so when two pool connections write (or one writes while another reads) the loser fails at once with SQLITE_BUSY / "database is locked" instead of waiting. With database/sql's multi-connection pool this can happen from ordinary concurrent HTTP requests (the dashboard fires several at once). Make the opener configure every pooled connection so concurrent writers wait and succeed.

Found by dev-qki-5 and its reviewer (2026-10-12): qki.5's concurrency test (PR #26) had to add `_pragma=busy_timeout` to its own DSN to pass.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12, autonomous scoper, no user input)
- Busy timeout 5000 ms on every connection, set by the opener (sqlite.Open), not by callers.
- Journal mode WAL for file-backed databases (readers no longer block the writer). In-memory DSNs cannot use WAL: the opener must keep working for `file::memory:?cache=shared&mode=memory` (used by DAL tests) and for an existing on-disk dev DB.
- Pragmas must apply to every connection the pool opens, not just the first (so: DSN `_pragma=` parameters for modernc.org/sqlite, or an equivalent per-connection hook; a one-off `db.Exec("PRAGMA ...")` after Open is NOT enough for busy_timeout).
- If the caller's DSN already sets a pragma (e.g. qki.5's test), the caller's value wins or the result is equivalent; no duplicate/conflicting pragma error.
- Standalone task, not in epic critical-qki: single user on a laptop, low urgency, cheap.

## Current behaviour
`sqlite.Open(dsn)` calls `sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)` + Ping with nothing else. CRITICAL_DSN defaults to `critical.db` (a bare path; `just dev` uses `../.dev/critical.db`). No busy_timeout, journal_mode or foreign_keys pragma anywhere in non-test code.

## Key interfaces
- `func Open(dsn string) (*DB, error)` in the storage/sqlite package keeps its signature; it normalises the DSN (bare path or `file:` URI) and adds the pragmas.
- `(*DB).InTx` / `WrapTx` / `Conn` unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every pooled connection reports `PRAGMA busy_timeout` = 5000 (test opens several connections, e.g. by holding one with db.Conn and checking another).
- [ ] A file-backed DB opened via Open reports `PRAGMA journal_mode` = wal.
- [ ] Test: two goroutines each run a write transaction (InTx or WrapTx) on the same file DB concurrently, the first holding its tx open briefly; both commit, no SQLITE_BUSY. The test fails on main without the fix.
- [ ] Open still works with a bare path, a `file:` URI with existing query params, and the shared in-memory DSN used by the DAL tests; existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] qki.5's concurrency test no longer needs its own `_pragma=busy_timeout` (remove it if PR #26 has merged by then; otherwise leave a note in the PR).
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Out of scope
- The hazard of a pool (non-ctx) write issued while an InTx transaction is open on the same request: busy_timeout only turns that into a 5 s wait then an error. If it shows up, file a separate bug to route the write through `sqlite.Conn(ctx, ...)`.
- Connection pool sizing (SetMaxOpenConns), foreign_keys pragma, synchronous mode tuning.
- fly.io / backup concerns (critical-8g1.5).

## Notes
No generated code (no migration, no .sql query), so no `just generate`. Not risky. Touches the same package as qki.5 / PR #26 but is not blocked by it.

Found while verifying critical-kiv.7 (unknown-AC attack, ADR 0012). (1) The tell-the-GM line shows critsFromAc even when it is far beyond any real AC (e.g. 'Critique dès CA 57'); the card should omit the crit part when critsFromAc is above the highest AC the rules allow (the bound comes from the server/ADR, not a TS constant). (2) Once the GM gives the AC there is no way back to 'unknown' on that attack.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The crit hint is shown only when a real AC can crit; the bound is server data or stated in ADR 0012.
- [ ] Decide (ADR 0012 note) whether an attack can return to unknown after the AC was given; implement if yes, latest-only like adjust.
- [ ] Unit tests; no new e2e unless a flow changes.
